items.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: I loved Dean Tolles. Everybody loved Dean Tolles. He tried to make me a businessman. He thought I would have the talent to go to Harvard business school... So he sent me to Boston to go to Harvard and take some interviews in the Harvard business school.

ctx.x: And what’s this business about — was it the president of the college at that time didn’t want no jazz on Sundays?

Sandy McEwen was a Presbyterian minister who, I don’t know it’d be very difficult to think of the things that he did like and approve of, but he certainly didn’t like us and approve of us, and he heard we were going to play a jazz session, I think it was at the Deke House. And he said, “No there’ll be no jazz on Sundays.” So we wrote a song called “Sandy Don’t ‘Low no Jazz on Sunday” you probably heard it. And it was a favorite of Ellie Wertimer’s. She would ask for that all the time. And in those days it was…
it was fine. Because he thought it would compete with chapel or something. Anyway. It had a happy ending.
